rationale:
bugs_open/283 round 9 — round 8's gating HIGH is closed AT THE SHARED GUARD, calibrated by the guard file's own rule; every other objection is answered with a fresh measurement or a bookkeeping fix in this submission.

(0) OPERATION SEMANTICS, first, because two prior_art objections turn on it: the edits describe the change set relative to pre-round-6 HEAD, and the code is COMMITTED to the shared branch (ffef54338 round 6; 35d2e0f9c judged-gate 5a/5b; 79fa79fb4 this round's shared-guard check) — this estate reviews after the fact by design (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2: HEAD is shared, holding a change back is not available). So 'add' is accurate for the new files at commit time, AND the cited census genuinely ran on the committed code. Fleet state, pod-probed this round on v1.0.1315 (digest-matched, revision 590ca3a20): repair_instance_scope_bindings present (5 hits — round 6's code rides the running binary), scriptStubRegression ABSENT (0 hits — this round's hardening awaits the next roll). Nothing exercises the judged branch or the repair batch until 486/487 are applied, and both are HOLD-gated on a roll carrying 35d2e0f9c+79fa79fb4 (the CONTINUE file's ancestry check names them).

(1) bug_historian HIGH — the shared guard stays blind. TRUE and CLOSED at componentRegressionIssues itself (79fa79fb4): new check 4, scriptStubRegression — the current row carries >=1000 bytes of inline (non-src) script, the replacement KEEPS inline script element(s), and every kept body is under 200 bytes. Blast radius enumerated by fresh grep this round: exactly three call sites — the two 283 arms and update_component_html (tool-improver's writeback), so tool-improver's whole-template LLM path is now covered too. The check is deliberately NARROWER than 'the script shrank', because the guard file's own calibration history shows why a mass check was tried and dropped: simulated per that file's rule over ALL 235 distinct consecutive component_versions transitions (plus current rows) — 0 legitimate transitions match, while a naive <30%-mass version of the check flagged two REAL legitimate shapes we then pinned as negative fixtures: the js-extraction pattern (tool-provocation-heat-rater: inline body moved behind src=, element remains, body empty BY DESIGN) and a genuine rework (tool-arena-interface v3→v4: a 7,189-byte clean program at 29.7% of its predecessor). The gutted control matches. Test: TestScriptStubRegression_calibratedShapes — control, both negative shapes, identity, growth.

(2) bug_historian MEDIUM — the 0.7 floor is unmeasured. NOW MEASURED against the actual judged pool (all 30 rows): worst comment+whitespace fraction of any script is 46.5% (mortgages-stamp-duty), so a brief-violating but harmless tidy could land at 0.54 and refuse to a human — the chosen failure direction, kept, because lowering the floor widens the band where genuine partial loss passes. Stated honestly in the constant's comment: NO structural check catches partial logic deletion that keeps every lookup (little mass moves); the per-tool behavioural oracle does — which is exactly why the owner ruled LMC-first (170 arithmetic checks per converted tool, moved in lockstep). The floor is the middle band's tripwire, 5a reference-parity the primary, the stub check the backstop, the oracle the behavioural verdict.

(3) editquality MEDIUM — the rollback guard was prose, not an edit. Fixed: the ROLLBACK file is now an explicit edit below. And the forward 486 guard's placement is as claimed: the double-apply DO/RAISE is the FIRST statement after BEGIN, BEFORE snapshot_agent, so a re-apply aborts without taking the mislabelled snapshot; the end-of-file DO/RAISE is the separate post-conditions verify.

(4) guardian MEDIUM — no before/after workflow diff. Attached: BEFORE (7 steps): ensure_site_record → apply_fix → check_needs_rerender ─fixed:true→ create_rerender → compose_note → append_note → complete (else compose_note). AFTER (13 steps): apply_fix → check_scope_route ─action==needs_script_scoping→ scope_script_llm → apply_judged_write → check_judged_result ─fixed:true→ check_needs_rerender / else→ judged_refusal(fail_work_item needs_human_review) → compose_note; check_scope_route else→ check_needs_rerender (unchanged); create_rerender → create_section_edit_delivery(owned placements) → compose_note. Every pre-existing step keeps its action and config except two next_step pointers (apply_fix, create_rerender), both guarded on their pre-image values in the UPDATE's WHERE.

(5) guardian MEDIUM — rerender fan-out unbounded. MEASURED CEILING: if every converted row were repaired, the template_changed fan-out reaches 56 generic pages across 22 sites; the actual batch repairs 27 rows, so fewer. PRECEDENT: the 2026-08-18 mechanical batch filed 72 page-scoped rerenders into the same queue in one afternoon and drained clean (53 complete / 15 cancelled / 4 failed, all accounted, §13.7) — this batch's worst case is smaller than a load the queue has already absorbed. Items enter at status 'triaged', priority 80, and drain through the existing dispatcher; no new concurrency is introduced.

(6) prior_art LOW — stale one-caller claim, dormant-machinery risk. Fresh this round: the action-reference query re-run (component-template-fixer remains the only workflow naming fix_component_template; zero sub_workflow references), the componentRegressionIssues caller grep above (3 sites), and a repo sweep for equivalent binding/scope-repair machinery outside the lane's files (grep IIFE/instance-scope/InstanceID across platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/ excluding the lane and its tests): hits are unrelated (thunder instance store, config loader) — no dormant equivalent exists to adopt.
